articles.title: Andhra Pradesh's Visakhapatnam ITI cluster becomes India's first to win PM-SETU approval
articles.content: Business Andhra Pradesh’s Visakhapatnam ITI cluster becomes India’s first to win PM-SETU approval; AM/NS India to invest Rs 200 crore upgrading four Government ITIs ITN · October 13, 2026 · 2 min read Quick Summary State, Centre and AM/NS India sign agreement to give students industry-grade skills for manufacturing jobs: Minister Nara Lokesh Visakhapatnam/Mumbai, October 12, 2026- The Government of Andhra Pradesh, the Government of India and ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India (AM/NS India) have signed… State, Centre and AM/NS India sign agreement to give students industry-grade skills for manufacturing jobs: Minister Nara Lokesh Visakhapatnam/Mumbai, October 12, 2026- The Government of Andhra Pradesh, the Government of India and ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India (AM/NS India) have signed a Shareholders’ Agreement to upgrade four Government Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the Visakhapatnam cluster under PM-SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs), with an approved investment of Rs 200 crore. The Visakhapatnam cluster’s Strategic Investment Plan was the first in the country to be approved by PM-SETU’s National Steering Committee. A dedicated Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) will be formed to manage the upgrades and operations. AM/NS India will hold 51% of it, and the Government of Andhra Pradesh and the Government of India will hold 24.5% each. Shri Nara Lokesh, Minister for IT, Electronics & Communication, Human Resource Development and Real-Time Governance, said: “Our priority is to ensure that Andhra Pradesh’s industrial growth creates opportunities for our young people. This partnership with AM/NS India will help students at four Government ITIs gain practical skills that employers need. By improving training facilities and bringing industry expertise into technical education, we aim to strengthen their employability and help them participate in the State’s growth.” Four ITIs, one hub The project covers: – Government ITI (Old), Kancharapalem, which will be the main training centre and will share its facilities and resources with the other three – Government ITI (Girls), Industrial Estate, Visakhapatnam – Government ITI, Bobbili – Government ITI, Narsipatnam What students will get AM/NS India will carry out the work with its academic and technical partner, the New Age Makers’ Institute of Technology (NAMTECH). The upgrades include modernised training facilities, workplace-relevant equipment, updated courses, new trades, hands-on practical training and stronger instructor training. Linking training more closely to industry requirements will make students more ready for jobs and help employers find skilled local candidates as Andhra Pradesh expands its industrial and manufacturing base. Ashutosh Telang, Director & Vice President – HR & Administration, AM/NS India, said: “Through this partnership, we will bring our manufacturing experience and NAMTECH’s technical education expertise to four Government ITIs in the Visakhapatnam cluster. Better facilities, hands-on learning and stronger instructor training will help students build skills that employers need.” Share: #Andhra Pradesh #Government #Visakhapatnam ITN We Live in a T-Shaped World- Broad knowledge across ecosystems is essential, but it’s the deep expertise of Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) that helps organizations leap forward. articles.title: Bayon is Hyundai's answer to Maruti Suzuki Victoris in India - NewsBytes
articles.content: Bookings for the car are now open Bayon is Hyundai's answer to Maruti Suzuki Victoris in India By Dwaipayan Roy Oct 13, 2026 01:09 pm What's the story Hyundai has officially unveiled the India-spec Bayon, a new addition to its SUV lineup. The vehicle will sit between the Venue and Creta models and is expected to strengthen Hyundai's foothold in the mid-size SUV segment. The company has opened bookings for the Bayon at ₹11,000 online and across authorized dealerships. Deliveries are expected during the festive season. Design A look at the design The Bayon adopts Hyundai's latest 'Art of Steel' design language with a layered front fascia and split headlamps. It gets slim LED daytime running lights on the bonnet's edge, while the main headlamp units are positioned lower down in the bumper. The SUV also features pronounced wheel arches, sharp character lines, and petal-style alloy wheels for a muscular look. Interior highlights The SUV gets a dual-screen setup with 12.3-inch displays The Bayon comes with a dual-screen setup of two 12.3-inch displays for the instrument cluster and infotainment system. The connected screens create a curved panoramic effect, giving the dashboard a modern look. It also gets Hyundai's Connected Car Navigation Cockpit (ccNC), accelerated by NVIDIA , which provides online navigation, split-screen view, personalized controls among other things. ADVERTISEMENT Tech integration It comes with a generative AI voice assistant The Bayon has Hyundai Motor India's first-ever Generative AI Voice Assistant, powered by Perplexity and SoundHound AI. The system can answer conversational queries about weather, travel plans, hotels/restaurants, places to visit, among other things. It also offers Hyundai Bluelink with over 70 connected car functions such as remote controls for various vehicle functions, vehicle status information and location-based services. ADVERTISEMENT Engine specs The vehicle draws power from a 1.5-liter petrol engine The Bayon is powered by a 1.5-liter, four-cylinder, naturally aspirated MPi petrol engine that makes 115hp and 144Nm of torque. The engine comes mated to either a six-speed manual gearbox or CVT, which Hyundai calls Intelligent Variable Transmission (IVT). The company has not announced the SUV's pricing yet, but it is expected to sit below the Creta in its lineup. Facebook Whatsapp Twitter Linkedin ADVERTISEMENT

articles.title: INS Vikrant replica unveiled in Kerala capital, celebrates India's naval prowess
articles.content: KOCHI, Oct 12: A detailed 1:24 scale replica of INS Vikrant, India's first indigenously built aircraft carrier, was dedicated to the Kerala capital at Museum Junction here on Monday, showcasing the country's growing naval capabilities and indigenous shipbuilding prowess. Kerala Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar dedicated the model in the presence of Vice Admiral Sameer Saxena, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Southern Naval Command. Admiral R. Harikumar (Retd), former Chief of the Naval Staff, Thiruvananthapuram Mayor V.V. Rajesh, senior officials of the Army, Navy, Air Force and Coast Guard, representatives of the Kerala government, naval veterans and other dignitaries attended the ceremony. The installation is part of an initiative to display scale models of INS Vikrant in various cities across the country, bringing India's maritime achievements closer to the public and highlighting the country's progress in indigenous defence manufacturing. Commissioned on September 2, 2022, by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, INS Vikrant is India's first aircraft carrier designed and built domestically and the largest warship constructed in the country. Built by Cochin Shipyard Limited in Kochi, the carrier represents a major milestone in India's warship design, engineering and construction capabilities and stands as a symbol of the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative. The meticulously crafted scale model reproduces the distinctive features and configuration of the aircraft carrier, offering visitors a closer view of the technological and engineering achievements behind the construction of the formidable warship. The dedication also highlights the enduring maritime association between the Indian Navy and the people of Kerala. The model is expected to inspire young people to pursue excellence in science, technology and engineering, while fostering awareness of India's maritime heritage and contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat.

articles.title: Vizag ITI cluster first in India to get PM-SETU nod - The New Indian Express
articles.content: VIJAYAWADA: In a landmark milestone for technical education and vocational training, AP’s Vizag Industrial Training Institute (ITI) cluster has become the first in India to secure approval under Union Government’s Rs 60,000-crore Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme. Solidifying the project’s execution framework, the State government, the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, and steel giant ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India (AM/NS India) signed a tripartite Shareholders’ Agreement (SHA) in Vizag to upgrade four government ITIs at an outlay of Rs 200 crore. Under the agreement, a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) will be established to oversee infrastructure upgrades, and day-to-day administration across the cluster. AM/NS India will hold a controlling 51 per cent stake in the SPV, while the State and Central government will each hold a 24.5% equity stake. “Our primary mandate is to ensure that AP’s expanding industrial footprint generates high-value employment for youth. Alliance with AM/NS India will equip students across four government ITIs with practical, job-ready skills required by modern manufacturing employers, integrating our workforce into the State’s growth story,” HRD Minister Nara Lokesh said. The Vizag cluster will operate under an integrated hub-and-spoke model. Government ITI (Old) at Kancharapalem will function as the main central training hub, sharing advanced machinery, labs, and instructional resources with three spoke institutes: Government ITI (Girls) at Industrial Estate, Vizag; Government ITI, Bobbili; and Government ITI, Narsipatnam. Execution of the upgrade will be led by AM/NS India alongside its technical and academic partner, the New Age Makers’ Institute of Technology (NAMTECH). Welcoming the partnership, Ashutosh Telang, Director & Vice President (HR & Administration) at AM/NS India, noted that blending manufacturing expertise with NAMTECH’s technical pedagogy will build a future-ready local candidate pool. The PM-SETU initiative aims to transform 1,000 Government ITIs and five National Skill Training Institutes nationwide. AM/NS India has signed parallel agreements covering nine ITIs in Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat, committing a total of Rs 440 crore. articles.title: INS Vikrant scale model unveiled at Museum Junction in Thiruvananthapuram
articles.content: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: The Indian Navy on Monday dedicated a large-scale model of INS Vikrant, India’s first indigenously built aircraft carrier, to Thiruvananthapuram, highlighting the country’s indigenous shipbuilding capabilities and the Navy’s longstanding maritime association with Kerala. Governor Rajendra Arlekar dedicated the model at a ceremony at the Museum Junction. The event was attended by Vice Admiral Sameer Saxena, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Southern Naval Command, Admiral R Harikumar (retd), Former Chief of Naval Staff, Mayor V V Rajesh, senior state government officials, veterans and other dignitaries. Built at the Cochin Shipyard Limited, INS Vikrant was commissioned into the Indian Navy on September 2, 2022, by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The aircraft carrier is a milestone in India’s efforts to develop indigenous capabilities in warship design and construction and a symbol of the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative. The 1:24 scale model reproduces the distinctive features and configuration of the aircraft carrier, offering visitors a closer look at the engineering and technological capabilities involved in building the warship.
